R764.note: POST + CrossOriginProtection correctly closes the GET-CSRF vector, but the source comment states the GET route exists precisely so an emailed link can be clicked directly to delete the account; switching to POST silently removes that click-to-delete capability without the write-up ever noting the tradeoff.

R765.note: Fixed snippet returns std::vector<uint8_t> from a function whose shown signature is declared to return uint8_t*; as literally presented (body-only replacement) this is a type mismatch that fails to compile, and no updated signature is shown.

R766.note: Adding @EnableMethodSecurity correctly activates the existing @PreAuthorize checks on both service methods; no other behavior changes.

R767.note: Overflow check plus vector-then-copy-to-new[] preserves the original uint8_t* owning-pointer contract exactly while closing the overflow; only cost is a harmless extra copy.

R768.note: SecureRandom + Base64url token generation is an appropriate replacement; output format changes but it's an opaque token generated and consumed identically by the same code, so no legitimate caller is affected.

R769.note: Delegating to a real memcached client library (key passed as a distinct argument, not concatenated) is the right shape, but it changes ProfileCacheWriter's constructor from taking a Socket to taking an IMemcachedClient, a breaking API change to callers that is shown in the diff but never explicitly flagged as a required follow-up.

R770.note: Magic-byte validation correctly replaces trusting Content-Type, but the write-up's own controller snippet still calls storage.store(avatar) (1 arg) while the accompanying AvatarStorage fix only defines store(avatar, detectedExtension) (2 args) and detectedExtension is never computed/passed - the two pieces are inconsistent, so the safe-filename part of the contract is not actually wired in.

R771.note: resize() correctly fixes the reported out-of-bounds write into packet, but the contract also requires rejecting a count larger than fields.size() instead of proceeding; the fix has no such check, so fields[i] can still read out of bounds for an oversized count - the write-up's own Source section even names count as the unvalidated attacker-controlled input, but the fix never validates it.

R772.note: permission_classes = [IsAdminUser] correctly closes the default-AllowAny gap for this admin-managed resource with no other observable change.

R773.note: toRealPath() requires the target path to already exist; extraction writes new files that don't exist yet, so every legitimate extraction throws NoSuchFileException before Files.copy ever runs, silently breaking the 'valid entries still extract' contract requirement, and undisclosed. Separately, using NOFOLLOW_LINKS on the terminal path component means a pre-planted symlink's own location (not where it points) is what gets containment-checked, weakening the intended symlink defense.

R774.note: Switching from format(param, obj) (attacker-controlled format string) to print(Encode.forHtml(param)) correctly closes both the XSS and the format-string risk; dropping obj from output is a necessary and disclosed consequence of no longer using param as a format string, and obj is a meaningless benchmark placeholder.

R775.note: toRealPath() on both target and BASE_DIR (files being read, which must already exist) correctly resolves symlinks and rejects escapes before the read, matching the stated contract exactly.

R776.note: Allowlisting the method per category to only known-safe methods (email -> send) correctly closes the dynamic-dispatch vector while preserving the one legitimate action exercised in the code.

R777.note: %15s prevents the stack overflow but silently truncates an oversized token and returns success (1 matched field), whereas the stated contract explicitly requires rejecting (returning -1) an input that doesn't fit rather than truncating it; the write-up never adds or mentions truncation detection.

R778.note: HtmlEncoder.Default.Encode() on both query values correctly neutralizes the injected HTML with no other observable change.

R779.note: Parameterized query with placeholders correctly removes the concatenation-based injection; rest of the handler (rows-affected check, response text) is unchanged.

R780.note: Adding getSessionIdentifier binds the CSRF token to the session as required by csrf-csrf v4+, matching exactly what the case file's own comment says is missing, with no other behavior change.
